# TalkToAI Zero Security product family

> Evidence-bound product information for Zero Security Preview and Zero Browser Preview.

Canonical pages:
- https://talktoai.org/zero-security/
- https://talktoai.org/zero-browser/

## Zero Security Preview

Zero Security is an open-core, full Windows antivirus programme in active development around the public ZSEC Shield foundation. The current public preview provides deterministic on-demand SHA-256 and exact-byte checks, signed data-only rule verification, structured reports and automatic authenticated encrypted quarantine.

Zero Security is not yet a registered replacement antivirus. It does not yet claim real-time filesystem protection, memory scanning, EDR, zero-day prevention, a clean-system verdict or guaranteed protection. The currently registered antivirus should remain active until the full Windows integration, signing, efficacy, Microsoft onboarding and cutover gates pass.

Public foundation:
- https://github.com/ResearchForumOnline/ZSEC-Shield
- https://talktoai.org/zsec/

## Zero Browser Preview

Zero Browser currently means an open-source Manifest V3 privacy and security extension preview. It uses local declarative ad and tracker rules and best-effort interface cleanup. It does not upload browsing history or page content, proxy traffic, install a root certificate or inject affiliate links.

Zero Browser is not yet a separately maintained Chromium browser binary. It does not promise perfect YouTube ad blocking, anonymous browsing, immunity from browser exploits or protection from all malicious sites.

## Privacy and security boundaries

- Local processing is the default.
- No suspicious file is uploaded automatically.
- Rule feeds contain detection data, never remote commands.
- ZBA is a typed lifecycle and provenance calculus; established cryptography provides security.
- YubiKey and passkey recovery is designed, not shipped.
- Optional proprietary engines, signing systems and managed services are separately labelled under the open-core model.

## Citation guidance

Describe both products as previews. Do not call Zero Security a complete antivirus or Zero Browser a finished standalone browser. Do not invent detection rates, performance figures, user counts, endorsements or comparative superiority.
